To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the creep curves for various loading ages can be represented by the form (t-t')F(t-t') where F is a function of t-t', and (2) this form of the creep function can be approximated by a function of the form f(t)+g(t) where f is the unit creep curve and g is a function of time.
the creep function for the C.E.B., International Recommendations, as proposed by Jordan and England, does not fit experimental data, and that a simpler form, already in use, is preferable.

the problem of the choice of a creep curve for the purpose of practical analysis.
the problem of the choice of a creep function for practical analysis of structures.
the problem of the creep of concrete under sustained loading.

the C.E.B.'s present creep function form is to be retained.
